#### Model Estimation {#sec-pmc-623}

[**AR(2) Model Parameter Estimates**]{#sec-pmc-623-ar2}

The following parameter estimates were computed for the AR(2) model based on the differenced data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pmc-623-ar2
#| tbl-cap: "AR(2) model fitting results for the differenced data"
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

aerosol <- read_table(
  here::here("datasets", "NEGIZ4.DAT"),
  skip = 50,
  col_names = c("Junk1", "Junk2", "ParticleSize", "Junk3", "Junk4")
) |>
  select(ParticleSize)

diff_y <- diff(aerosol$ParticleSize)

fit_ar2 <- arima(diff_y, order = c(2, 0, 0), method = "ML")
ar2_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_ar2)))

tibble(
  Source = c("Intercept", "AR1", "AR2"),
  Estimate = c(fit_ar2$coef["intercept"], fit_ar2$coef["ar1"], fit_ar2$coef["ar2"]),
  `Standard Error` = c(ar2_se["intercept"], ar2_se["ar1"], ar2_se["ar2"])
) |>
  mutate(
    Lower = Estimate - qnorm(0.975) * `Standard Error`,
    Upper = Estimate + qnorm(0.975) * `Standard Error`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| include: false
n_ar2 <- length(diff_y)
resid_sd_ar2 <- sqrt(fit_ar2$sigma2)
```

Number of Observations: `r n_ar2`

Degrees of Freedom: `r n_ar2` - 3 = `r n_ar2 - 3`

Residual Standard Deviation: `r round(resid_sd_ar2, 4)`

Both AR parameters are significant since the confidence intervals do not contain zero.

The model for the differenced data, $Y_t$, is an AR(2) model,

$$ Y_{t} = -0.4064 Y_{t-1} - 0.1649 Y_{t-2} - 0.0050 \, , $$

with $\sigma =$ `r round(resid_sd_ar2, 4)`.

It is often more convenient to express the model in terms of the original data, $X_t$, rather than the differenced data. From the definition of the difference, $Y_t = X_t - X_{t-1}$, we can make the appropriate substitutions into the above equation,

$$ X_{t} - X_{t-1} = -0.4064 (X_{t-1} - X_{t-2}) - 0.1649 (X_{t-2} - X_{t-3}) - 0.0050 \, , $$

to arrive at the model in terms of the original series,

$$ X_{t} = 0.5936 X_{t-1} + 0.2415 X_{t-2} + 0.1649 X_{t-3} - 0.0050 \, . $$

[**MA(1) Model Parameter Estimates**]{#sec-pmc-623-ma1}

Alternatively, the parameter estimates for an MA(1) model based on the differenced data are the following.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pmc-623-ma1
#| tbl-cap: "MA(1) model fitting results for the differenced data"
#| code-fold: true
fit_ma1 <- arima(diff_y, order = c(0, 0, 1), method = "ML")
ma1_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_ma1)))

tibble(
  Source = c("Intercept", "MA1"),
  Estimate = c(fit_ma1$coef["intercept"], fit_ma1$coef["ma1"]),
  `Standard Error` = c(ma1_se["intercept"], ma1_se["ma1"])
) |>
  mutate(
    Lower = Estimate - qnorm(0.975) * `Standard Error`,
    Upper = Estimate + qnorm(0.975) * `Standard Error`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| include: false
n_ma1 <- length(diff_y)
resid_sd_ma1 <- sqrt(fit_ma1$sigma2)
```

Number of Observations: `r n_ma1`

Degrees of Freedom: `r n_ma1` - 2 = `r n_ma1 - 2`

Residual Standard Deviation: `r round(resid_sd_ma1, 4)`

The model for the differenced data, $Y_t$, is an ARIMA(0,1,1) model,

$$ Y_{t} = a_{t} - 0.3921 a_{t-1} - 0.0051 \, , $$

with $\sigma =$ `r round(resid_sd_ma1, 4)`.

It is often more convenient to express the model in terms of the original data, $X_t$, rather than the differenced data. Making the appropriate substitutions into the above equation,

$$ X_{t} - X_{t-1} = a_{t} - 0.3921 a_{t-1} - 0.0051 \, , $$

we arrive at the model in terms of the original series,

$$ X_{t} = X_{t-1} + a_{t} - 0.3921 a_{t-1} - 0.0051 \, . $$
